summary: The board's own logic is the RCA CDP1869/1870 VIS video/sound pair plus glue. The core models them as one combined 'vis_*' block, the same way MAME's cdp1869_device does. Its char-RAM and PCB addressing copies the cidelsa.cpp callback expressions, including MAME's BIT(pma,10)?0xff hack, and the pcb/char asymmetry between cidelsa_charram_r and cidelsa_pcb_r. Colour goes through a software-style pen index (color + (bkg+1)*8) that a separate palette module decodes back into RGB with luma weights. Video is generated per pixel against a raster counter, which is normal FPGA practice rather than evidence either way. The Draco sound glue wires the COP402 G pins straight to the AY BDIR/BC1 pins the way the board would, but that module belongs to a sibling machine.

findings.signal: char RAM address copied from MAME callback
findings.note: column = pma[10] ? 8'hff : pmd; addr = ((column<<3)|(cma&7)) & 11'h7ff matches MAME line for line, CIDELSA_CHARRAM_MASK included. The 0xff substitution is MAME's way of modelling the addressing, not a gate network.

The display path uses the column-hacked index for char data but raw pmd for the PCB address, and a draco flag swaps to raw pmd for both. That reproduces exactly how MAME's cidelsa/draco callbacks differ.

findings.signal: PCB returned through a latched side-effect variable
findings.note: pcb_in0 is captured during CPU char-RAM reads and spliced into IN0 bit 7. This mirrors MAME setting m_cdp1869_pcb as a side effect of the char read and returning it through a PORT_READ_LINE.

findings.mame_ref: sound/cdp1869.cpp get_pen / palette init (device file not provided; recalled)
findings.note: The COL-mux into {r,b,g} is folded into a 7-bit pen (cfc ? color3+((bkg+1)<<3) : color3). vis_palette then undoes it with (pen-8)>>3 and (pen-8)&7, and luma values 76/150/28 are 0.30/0.59/0.11 weights. That is an emulator palette table, not the 1870's RGB/luminance output pins.

findings.signal: VIS register semantics in emulator form
findings.note: On OUT5, pma is cleared unless cmem is set, hma is masked to addr[10:2]<<2, and a separate 'get_pma' mux handles dblpage. These are register-update rules written as assignments, with names matching the MAME device's accessors, rather than latch and counter structure.

findings.signal: single combined VIS device, chip split ignored
findings.note: The board has two chips, the CDP1869 (address/sound) and the CDP1870 (video/colour). The core instead divides function the way MAME's one merged cdp1869_device does: regs, page/char RAM, video, palette and sound. No module carries the 1869/1870 pin interface.

lines/height/cols/rows come from a case table and pmemsize = (cols*rows)<<dblpage<<line16 with wrap-by-subtraction (page_a0 >= pmemsize ? page_a0-pmemsize). This is arithmetic carried over from the emulator's helper functions, not the counter carry and reload logic a chip would use.

Page, char and pcb fetches run off H/V counters with a 2-stage pipeline instead of MAME's per-frame batch draw. The constants (360x312, display 54-300 / 44-260, predisplay 43) are CDP1869 PAL timing that both sides must share, so this is ordinary FPGA raster practice.

findings.signal: PRD inverted to INT and EF1; Q into the PCB RAM
findings.note: The inverted PRD drives both the INT and EF1 lines, and the CPU Q line is written into the 1-bit PCB RAM. This is board wiring that MAME and the core both reproduce.
The ROM, NVRAM, char RAM and page RAM ranges and the IN0/IN1 ports match MAME's address map, as any correct core must.

findings.signal: COP402 G pins wired to AY BDIR/BC1
findings.note: The core drives the jt49 bus pins straight from G0/G1, where MAME decodes G with a switch statement and keeps m_psg_latch. That is board-style wiring, but it lives in the sibling Draco machine, not Destroyer.
Tone and noise are divide-by counters and a 17-bit LFSR clocked from the pixel enable, which is closer to chip structure than a sample-rate formula. It is small and of uncertain provenance.
